A repository-relative glob over `*`, `**`, brace alternations and literal segments. Labeled query→doc retrieval-quality set for FR2 (spec Q13). Split into 'tune' (calibrate RRF k + bge query prefix) and 'held' (the pre-registered acceptance gate — measured once). Categories: 'zero-overlap' (target shares ~no tokens with the query while a distractor does — only vector can retrieve it; tests D20/C2b), 'paraphrase' (low lexical overlap), 'long-doc' (target is long, matching passage buried — tests C3 length bias), 'lexical-strong' (lexical already wins — the regression budget guards these). Authored solo, so blinding is partial (see eval-methodology.md); the mechanically-enforceable parts (zero-overlap pairs, long-doc pairs, tune/held split, pre-registered bar) are done rigorously.

value.title: Session Token Refresh
value.content: When an access token expires, the client silently obtains a new one by presenting its long-lived refresh token to the refresh endpoint, which mints a fresh short-lived token. The old token is revoked. This keeps a signed-in user from being interrupted while bounding the blast radius of a leaked token.

value.title: OAuth Device Flow
value.content: The device authorization grant lets input-constrained devices like TVs obtain user consent. The device shows a short code; the user visits a verification page on a second device and approves. The device then polls the token endpoint until consent is granted.

value.title: Login Rate Limiting
value.content: Repeated failed sign-in attempts from one source are throttled with exponential backoff and temporary lockout to slow credential-stuffing and brute-force password guessing without locking out legitimate users for long.

value.title: Password Reset
value.content: A user who forgot their password requests a reset link sent to their verified email. The link carries a single-use, time-limited token; following it lets them choose a new password and invalidates old sessions.

value.title: BM25 Ranking
value.content: BM25 scores how well a document matches query keywords using term frequency with saturation and inverse document frequency, normalized by document length. It is the workhorse of keyword search but matches words, not meaning.

value.title: Vector Embeddings
value.content: A sentence-transformer maps text to a dense vector so that passages with similar meaning land near each other in space. Retrieval by cosine distance then surfaces conceptually related content even when it shares no words with the query.

value.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
value.content: To merge two ranked lists whose scores live on incompatible scales, sum one over a constant plus rank across the lists. Because only rank position matters, there is no need to normalize an unbounded keyword score against a bounded similarity.

value.title: Query Autocomplete
value.content: As the user types in the search box, a prefix index suggests likely completions ordered by popularity and recency so they can jump to a known destination without finishing the word.

value.title: Blue-Green Deploys
value.content: Two identical production environments run side by side. New code goes live in the idle one; once it passes smoke checks the router cuts all traffic over instantly. If something breaks, flip the router back to roll the release back in seconds.

value.title: Database Migrations
value.content: Schema changes ship as ordered, versioned scripts applied forward at deploy time. Expand-then-contract steps keep each change backward compatible so the application and the schema can roll out independently with no downtime.

value.title: Incident Runbook
value.content: When an alert fires, page the on-call engineer, open a dedicated channel, declare a severity, and work the triage checklist: confirm impact, mitigate first, find the cause second, and write a blameless postmortem after the service recovers.

value.title: Observability
value.content: Traces, metrics, and structured logs together let an operator ask new questions of a running system without shipping new code. Spans stitch a request across services; histograms surface tail latency; logs carry the detail.

value.title: Conflict Resolution
value.content: Two people editing the same paragraph at once never clobber each other because every keystroke is a commutative operation that merges deterministically. The data structure converges to the same state on every replica regardless of order.

value.title: Markdown Pipeline
value.content: A document is parsed into an abstract syntax tree, transformed through a chain of handlers that normalize and enrich nodes, and serialized back to canonical markdown so the round trip is stable and lossless.

value.title: Backlinks
value.content: Every wiki-style link from one note to another is indexed in both directions, so opening a page shows which other pages point at it. Dense backlinking is how the knowledge base stays navigable as it grows.

value.title: Token Bucket Algorithm
value.content: A token bucket refills at a fixed rate up to a cap. Each request removes a token; an empty bucket means the caller is rate limited. It smooths bursts while bounding the long-run rate.

value.title: Refresh Button
value.content: Pressing refresh re-fetches the current view from the server and repaints it, discarding any stale cached copy the browser was showing.

value.title: Vector Graphics
value.content: Vector graphics describe images as scalable shapes — paths, curves, and fills — instead of a grid of pixels, so they stay crisp at any size and export to SVG.

value.title: Cold Storage
value.content: Infrequently accessed data is moved to cheap, slow archival storage with long retrieval times, trading latency for cost on records that are kept for compliance but rarely read.

value.title: Team Onboarding
value.content: A new engineer's first week: get accounts provisioned, clone the repo, run the app locally, ship a tiny change behind a flag, and pair with a buddy who answers questions and reviews the first pull request.

value.title: Platform Architecture Overview
value.content: This document surveys the whole platform end to end. The edge layer terminates TLS and routes requests to stateless application servers, which talk to a primary datastore and a read-replica fleet. Background workers drain a durable queue for asynchronous jobs like sending email and rebuilding derived indexes. The collaboration core keeps every document as a conflict-free replicated data type so concurrent editors converge without a central lock; a file watcher mirrors changes to disk and a shadow repository tracks per-writer work in progress. Search is served by an in-memory keyword index, and — when enabled — an on-device embedding model adds a meaning-based signal so a query about a concept can find a passage that never uses the query's exact words. Observability spans, metrics, and logs flow to a local sink for diagnosis. Releases roll out blue-green: a fresh environment goes live behind the router and the previous one stays warm for instant rollback. Secrets live in the OS keychain, never on disk. The whole system is designed local-first: a single user's machine runs the full stack with no cloud dependency, and nothing about a private note ever leaves the device.

value.title: Engineering Handbook
value.content: Our engineering culture in one page. We write small, reversible changes and ship them behind flags so a risky idea can be turned off without a deploy. Code review is mandatory and kind: reviewers explain the why, authors assume good faith. Tests describe behavior, not implementation, so a refactor that preserves behavior keeps them green. We measure before optimizing and keep a calibrated performance budget. On call rotates weekly; when an incident happens we mitigate before we investigate and we never blame a person for a system that let a mistake through. To undo a bad release we flip production traffic back to the previous environment, which restores service in seconds while we diagnose. Documentation lives next to the code and is treated as part of the change, not an afterthought. Above all we optimize for the long-run health of the codebase over the short-run convenience of any single change.

if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == push ]]; then
  case "${BETA_CUT:-push}" in
    push)

      ;;

      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
elif [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == workflow_dispatch ]]; then
  if [[ -z "${CUT_SHA:-}" ]]; then
    echo "ref=$GITHUB_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [[ ! "$CUT_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
    echo "::error::The sha input is not a full 40-character lowercase commit SHA. Refusing to cut."
    exit 1
  fi
  if ! status=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/compare/${CUT_SHA}...main" --jq .status); then
    echo "::error::Could not compare ${CUT_SHA} with main, so this run cannot confirm main contains it. Refusing to cut."

  if [[ "$status" != ahead && "$status" != identical ]]; then
    echo "::error::${CUT_SHA} is not reachable from main (compare status ${status}). Refusing to cut a commit main does not contain."
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "ref=$CUT_SHA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "Cutting the beta at ${CUT_SHA}, given by the sha input; main contains it (compare status ${status})." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi

# then a descendant of the release commit rather than an ancestor.
#
# The workflow file comes from the DEFAULT branch, but the checkout is
# the RELEASE ref — so for any tag cut before this selector landed, the
# script is simply absent from the workspace. Materialize it from the
# same commit the workflow itself came from, falling back to the
# checked-out copy. Pairing the two is what lets a re-fire on a stale
# tag run CURRENT release machinery rather than whatever was frozen in
# that tag, which is the only way re-firing a blocked release can ever
# clear it. fetch-depth:0 in checkout has $GITHUB_SHA. The native-set
# judge that decides what staging may package comes the same way.
judge="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/assert-native-set.mjs"
if ! git show "$GITHUB_SHA:.github/scripts/assert-native-set.mjs" > "$judge" 2>/dev/null; then
  cp .github/scripts/assert-native-set.mjs "$judge" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
selector="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/select-native-config-prebuild.mjs"
if ! git show "$GITHUB_SHA:.github/scripts/select-native-config-prebuild.mjs" > "$selector" 2>/dev/null; then
  cp .github/scripts/select-native-config-prebuild.mjs "$selector" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if [ ! -s "$selector" ]; then
  judge_staging "native-config prebuild selector is missing at $GITHUB_SHA and in the release checkout"
fi
nc_err="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/native-config-select.err"
if ! selection=$(node "$selector" 2>"$nc_err"); then
  reason=$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$nc_err" | sed 's/  *$//')
  judge_staging "${reason:-could not select a native-config prebuild run}"
fi
# Assert the WHOLE shape, on ONE line. Testing for a tab anywhere is
# not enough: a stray line ahead of the real answer still contains a
# tab, so it passes and leaves that noise in run_id, which only
# surfaces later as a confusing `gh run download` failure. Anchoring
# the whole value is what actually rejects it. The message is flattened
# because ::error:: annotations are single-line — an interpolated
# multi-line value would truncate the page.
selection_shape='^[0-9]+'$'\t''[0-9a-f]{7,40}$'
if [[ ! $selection =~ $selection_shape ]]; then
  flattened=$(printf '%s' "$selection" | tr '\n' ' ')
  judge_staging "native-config prebuild selector returned an unusable answer: $flattened"
fi
run_id="${selection%%$'\t'*}"
head_sha="${selection##*$'\t'}"

if ! download_bindings "$run_id"; then
  judge_staging "could not download native-config-bindings-all from run $run_id after 3 attempts"
fi
find /tmp/nc-bindings -name '*.node' -exec cp -f {} packages/native-config/ \;
count=$(find packages/native-config -maxdepth 1 -name '*.node' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
echo "staged $count native-config prebuilt binaries from run $run_id (commit $head_sha)"
judge_staging "staged $count native-config binaries from run $run_id (commit $head_sha)"

value.name: Resolve -beta.N counter

value.name: Download the tarball the build job packed

value.run:
set -euo pipefail

if [[ "$ACTION" == "publish-stable" ]]; then
  TAG=latest
  VERSION="$STABLE_VERSION"
else
  TAG=beta
  VERSION="$BETA_VERSION"
fi

shopt -s nullglob
tarballs=("$PACKAGE_DIR"/*.tgz)
if (( ${#tarballs[@]} != 1 )); then
  echo "::error::The build job's npm-package artifact holds ${#tarballs[@]} tarballs, not one. Refusing to publish."
  exit 1
fi
TARBALL="${tarballs[0]}"
pacote="$(npm root -g)/npm/node_modules/pacote"
read_status=0
manifest=$(node -e '
  const fail = (status) => (error) => {
    process.stderr.write(JSON.stringify(String(error && error.message)) + "\n");
    process.exit(status);
  };
  let reading;
  try {
    reading = require(process.argv[1])
      .manifest("file:" + process.argv[2], { fullMetadata: true, fullReadJson: true });
  } catch (error) {
    fail(2)(error);
  }
  reading.then((manifest) => process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(manifest)), fail(1));
' "$pacote" "$TARBALL") || read_status=$?
if (( read_status == 2 )); then
  echo "::error::npm's pacote did not load from ${pacote}, or threw before opening the tarball; its reason is printed above, JSON-encoded. Refusing to publish."
  exit 1
fi
if (( read_status != 0 )); then
  echo "::error::npm cannot read the packed tarball's manifest; its reason is printed above, JSON-encoded. Refusing to publish."
  exit 1
fi
if ! jq -e --arg name "$PACKAGE_NAME" --arg version "$VERSION" \
  '.name == $name and .version == $version and ((.publishConfig // {}) | keys - ["access"] | length == 0)' \
  <<<"$manifest" >/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::The packed tarball's manifest, as npm reads it, is $(jq -c '{name, version, publishConfig}' <<<"$manifest"). This job publishes only ${PACKAGE_NAME}@${VERSION}, whose publishConfig may set access and nothing else. Refusing to publish."
  exit 1
fi

if [[ "$(npm view "${PACKAGE_NAME}@${VERSION}" version 2>/dev/null || true)" == "$VERSION" ]]; then
  echo "::notice::${PACKAGE_NAME}@${VERSION} is already on npm; nothing to publish."
  exit 0
fi

echo "Publishing with --tag ${TAG} (VERSION=${VERSION})"
npm publish "$TARBALL" --access public --tag "$TAG" --provenance --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/

IFS=',' read -ra toks <<<"$REQUIRED"

  case "$t" in
    mac|windows|linux) ;;

fi

  cp .github/scripts/select-native-config-prebuild.mjs "$selector" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if [ ! -s "$selector" ]; then
  judge_staging "native-config prebuild selector is missing at $GITHUB_SHA and in the release checkout"
fi
nc_err="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/native-config-select.err"
if ! selection=$(node "$selector" 2>"$nc_err"); then
  reason=$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$nc_err" | sed 's/  *$//')
  judge_staging "${reason:-could not select a native-config prebuild run}"
fi
# Assert the WHOLE shape, on ONE line. Testing for a tab anywhere is
# not enough: a stray line ahead of the real answer still contains a
# tab, so it passes and leaves that noise in run_id, which only
# surfaces later as a confusing `gh run download` failure. Anchoring
# the whole value is what actually rejects it. The message is flattened
# because ::error:: annotations are single-line — an interpolated

value.name: Prepare signing keychain (CSC_KEYCHAIN)
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
KEYCHAIN_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/ok-signing.keychain-db"
KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD="$(head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64)"
echo "::add-mask::$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD"
CERT_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/ok-signing.p12"
trap 'rm -f "$CERT_PATH"' EXIT

# CSC_LINK is bare base64 of the .p12 (workflow header). macOS
# `base64 -i` wraps lines, hence the whitespace strip.
printf '%s' "$CSC_LINK" | tr -d '[:space:]' | base64 -d > "$CERT_PATH"
if [[ ! -s "$CERT_PATH" ]]; then
  echo "::error::CSC_LINK did not materialize a .p12 (empty after decode). Re-export with 'base64 -i developer-id.p12 | pbcopy' and paste the single-line output."
  exit 1
fi

security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN_PATH"
# No lock timeout: sign + notarize runs well past the 5 min default.
security set-keychain-settings "$KEYCHAIN_PATH"
security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN_PATH"
security import "$CERT_PATH" -k "$KEYCHAIN_PATH" -P "$CSC_KEY_PASSWORD" \
  -T /usr/bin/codesign -T /usr/bin/productbuild >/dev/null
# The call electron-builder gets wrong: -k is the KEYCHAIN password.
# Without this, codesign blocks on a GUI prompt for the private key.
security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s \
  -k "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN_PATH" >/dev/null

# Search list: this keychain first, then electron-builder's bundled
# Apple root + intermediate certs (it adds these itself on the
# CSC_LINK path so the Developer ID chain validates offline), then
# whatever was already listed. `list-keychains -s` REPLACES the list.
ROOT_CERTS="$(node -e '
  const path = require("path");
  const eb = path.dirname(require.resolve("electron-builder/package.json"));
  const lib = path.dirname(require.resolve("app-builder-lib/package.json", { paths: [eb] }));
  process.stdout.write(path.join(lib, "certs", "root_certs.keychain"));
')"
if [[ ! -f "$ROOT_CERTS" ]]; then
  echo "::error::app-builder-lib's bundled root_certs.keychain is not at $ROOT_CERTS; its certs layout may have moved in a dependency bump."
  exit 1
fi
if ! LISTED="$(security list-keychains -d user)"; then
  echo "::error::security list-keychains failed; refusing to replace the user search list blind."
  exit 1
fi
EXISTING=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
  line="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
  line="${line%\"}"
  line="${line#\"}"
  [[ -n "$line" ]] && EXISTING+=("$line")
done <<<"$LISTED"
# `${arr[@]+...}`: the runner's bash 3.2 treats an empty array as
# unbound under set -u.
security list-keychains -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN_PATH" "$ROOT_CERTS" ${EXISTING[@]+"${EXISTING[@]}"}

IDENTITIES="$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning "$KEYCHAIN_PATH")"
echo "$IDENTITIES"
if ! grep -q '"Developer ID Application' <<<"$IDENTITIES"; then
  echo "::error::No valid 'Developer ID Application' identity in the staged keychain. Either the CSC_LINK .p12 / CSC_KEY_PASSWORD pair is wrong, or the cert chain does not validate on this runner. The full identity list is above."
  exit 1
fi
echo "CSC_KEYCHAIN=$KEYCHAIN_PATH" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

value.run:
# extraMetadata.version override: kept as defense-in-depth so the
# Desktop's app.getVersion() / Info.plist / DMG filename / manifest
# `version` all agree with the tag even if the on-disk override
# step above is skipped, dropped, or partially applied. Under the
# zero-commit-bump cadence the on-disk versions ALWAYS lag the
# release tag, so this override is never a no-op for the Desktop's
# own metadata. But it does NOT reach the CLI bundle's
# compile-time-inlined PACKAGE_VERSION, which is baked in at Build
# time, so the workspace-wide on-disk override step above is what
# makes it match the tag. See PRD-6650.
set -euo pipefail
WRAPPER="${RUNNER_TEMP}/retry-transient.mjs"
WRAPPER_TMP="${WRAPPER}.tmp.$$"
export DESKTOP_PACKAGER="${RUNNER_TEMP}/package-desktop.mjs"
PACKAGER_TMP="${DESKTOP_PACKAGER}.tmp.$$"
trap 'rm -f "$WRAPPER_TMP" "$PACKAGER_TMP"' EXIT
materialized=false
for materialize_attempt in 1 2 3; do
  if git -C "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA" &&
     git -C "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" show "$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA:.github/scripts/retry-transient.mjs" > "$WRAPPER_TMP" &&
     [[ -s "$WRAPPER_TMP" ]] &&
     git -C "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" show "$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA:.github/scripts/package-desktop.mjs" > "$PACKAGER_TMP" &&
     [[ -s "$PACKAGER_TMP" ]] &&
     mv "$PACKAGER_TMP" "$DESKTOP_PACKAGER" &&
     mv "$WRAPPER_TMP" "$WRAPPER"; then
    materialized=true
    break
  fi
  rm -f "$WRAPPER_TMP" "$PACKAGER_TMP"
  if [[ "$materialize_attempt" -lt 3 ]]; then
    materialize_delay=$((materialize_attempt * 5))
    echo "::warning::Retry wrapper materialization attempt ${materialize_attempt}/3 failed; retrying in ${materialize_delay}s."
    sleep "$materialize_delay"
  fi
done
if [[ "$materialized" != true ]]; then
  echo "::error::Failed to materialize retry wrapper from workflow SHA ${GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA} after 3 attempts."
  exit 1
fi
echo "::notice::Retry wrapper materialized from workflow SHA ${GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA}."

value.name: Smoke the packaged DMG (FR5b)
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
CONFIG="packages/desktop/playwright.packaged.config.ts"
DRIVER=".github/scripts/smoke-packaged-dmg.mjs"
if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG" || ! -f "$DRIVER" ]]; then
  echo "verdict=skipped" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "reason=the smoke harness is not present at ${RELEASE_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "::notice::DMG smoke gate absent at ${RELEASE_TAG} (ref predates the harness) — releasing without it. Later tags carry the gate."
  exit 0
fi
# The harness is CI tooling, not release content, so take it from the
# workflow's own SHA rather than the release checkout — same reasoning
# as the finalize/alert jobs, which check out $GITHUB_SHA outright.
# Without this, a fix to the copy logic only reaches tags cut AFTER it
# lands, so every tag already cut stays permanently unreleasable:
# promote-stable tags the stable at the beta's SHA, and a soaked beta
# is by definition older than the fix. Overlaying only these files
# keeps the config and the smoke tests themselves pinned to the
# release, which is right — they assert the app's behavior.
# Deliberately AFTER the absent-gate check above, so a ref predating
# the harness still releases ungated rather than being newly gated by
# a file it never carried. Best-effort: on failure keep the tag's
# copy rather than block.
if git fetch --depth=1 origin "$GITHUB_SHA" >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
   git checkout "$GITHUB_SHA" -- "$DRIVER" .github/scripts/dmg-mount.mjs test-support/playwright-final-failure-annotations.ts 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::notice::Smoke harness taken from ${GITHUB_SHA} rather than ${RELEASE_TAG}."
else
  echo "::warning::Could not read the smoke harness from ${GITHUB_SHA}; using the copy carried by ${RELEASE_TAG}."
fi
# `.dmg.blockmap` sorts next to `.dmg`; match only the bundle itself.
# `|| true` keeps `set -e` from killing the step when dist-desktop is
# absent — the explicit empty-DMG guard below owns that message.
DMG="$(find packages/desktop/dist-desktop -maxdepth 1 -name '*.dmg' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)"
if [[ -z "$DMG" ]]; then
  echo "verdict=error" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "reason=electron-builder produced no .dmg to smoke" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "::error::No .dmg found under packages/desktop/dist-desktop for ${RELEASE_TAG}; refusing to publish an unverified release."
  exit 1
fi
echo "Smoking ${DMG} for ${RELEASE_TAG}…"
# The driver writes verdict= / reason= to GITHUB_OUTPUT itself and
# exits 0 / 1 / 2 for pass / fail / error, so this step fails closed
# on both non-pass verdicts without any branching here.
node "$DRIVER" "$DMG"

value.run:
set -euo pipefail
WRAPPER="${RUNNER_TEMP}/retry-transient.mjs"
WRAPPER_TMP="${WRAPPER}.tmp.$$"
export DESKTOP_PACKAGER="${RUNNER_TEMP}/package-desktop.mjs"
PACKAGER_TMP="${DESKTOP_PACKAGER}.tmp.$$"
trap 'rm -f "$WRAPPER_TMP" "$PACKAGER_TMP"' EXIT
materialized=false
for materialize_attempt in 1 2 3; do
  if git -C "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA" &&
     git -C "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" show "$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA:.github/scripts/retry-transient.mjs" > "$WRAPPER_TMP" &&
     [[ -s "$WRAPPER_TMP" ]] &&
     git -C "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" show "$GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA:.github/scripts/package-desktop.mjs" > "$PACKAGER_TMP" &&
     [[ -s "$PACKAGER_TMP" ]] &&
     mv "$PACKAGER_TMP" "$DESKTOP_PACKAGER" &&
     mv "$WRAPPER_TMP" "$WRAPPER"; then
    materialized=true
    break
  fi
  rm -f "$WRAPPER_TMP" "$PACKAGER_TMP"
  if [[ "$materialize_attempt" -lt 3 ]]; then
    materialize_delay=$((materialize_attempt * 5))
    echo "::warning::Retry wrapper materialization attempt ${materialize_attempt}/3 failed; retrying in ${materialize_delay}s."
    sleep "$materialize_delay"
  fi
done
if [[ "$materialized" != true ]]; then
  echo "::error::Failed to materialize retry wrapper from workflow SHA ${GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA} after 3 attempts."
  exit 1
fi
echo "::notice::Retry wrapper materialized from workflow SHA ${GITHUB_WORKFLOW_SHA}."
node "$WRAPPER" --label "electron-builder (Linux ${LINUX_TARGETS})" --max-attempts 3 --deadline-epoch-ms "$PACKAGING_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS" --shell -- "$PKG_CMD"

{
  echo "EXPECTED_ASSETS<<OK_INVENTORY_EOF"

value.name: Assert the complete cross-platform inventory
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
mapfile -t expected <<<"$EXPECTED_ASSETS"
echo "Staged files:"
ls -la release-assets/
missing=()
for f in "${expected[@]}"; do
  [[ -f "release-assets/${f}" ]] || missing+=("$f")
done
if [[ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "::error::Refusing to publish an incomplete release — missing from the staged assets: ${missing[*]}"
  exit 1
fi
# Unexpected extras are an error too: a stray builder-debug.yml or
# half-renamed artifact reaching the Release would be served to
# real update clients. Present files are validated against the
# ALLOWED universe (all platforms), not the required subset, so a
# healthy non-required platform's assets pass while junk fails.
mapfile -t allowed <<<"$ALLOWED_ASSETS"
for f in release-assets/*; do
  base="$(basename "$f")"
  found=0
  for e in "${allowed[@]}"; do
    [[ "$base" == "$e" ]] && found=1 && break
  done
  if [[ "$found" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "::error::Unexpected file staged for release upload: ${base}. Add it to the known-asset universe or fix the packaging job's upload globs."
    exit 1
  fi
done
echo "All ${#expected[@]} required assets staged; every staged file is a known asset."

value.name: Upload assets to the GitHub Release
value.run:
# -e deliberately omitted: the while/if retry loop owns every exit
# code explicitly; adding -e would abort the step on the first
# failed attempt instead of retrying it.
set -uo pipefail
attempt=1
max_attempts=3
while true; do
  # `timeout` bounds a hung upload (headers accepted, body stalled)
  # so it becomes a retryable failure instead of silently eating
  # the whole job budget: 3×300s attempts + 60s+120s backoffs fit
  # the 20-minute job timeout with headroom.
  if timeout 300 gh release upload "$RELEASE_TAG" release-assets/* --clobber; then
    echo "Uploaded all assets to ${RELEASE_TAG} on attempt ${attempt}."
    break
  fi
  if [ "${attempt}" -ge "${max_attempts}" ]; then
    echo "::error::gh release upload failed after ${max_attempts} attempts."
    exit 1
  fi
  backoff=$((attempt * 60))
  echo "::warning::gh release upload attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying in ${backoff}s (secondary-rate-limit cooldown is 60-120s)."
  sleep "${backoff}"
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
done

mapfile -t expected <<<"$EXPECTED_ASSETS"
missing=()
for f in "${expected[@]}"; do
  grep -qxF "$f" <<<"$uploaded" || missing+=("$f")
done
if [[ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "::error::Post-upload verification failed — the Release is missing: ${missing[*]}"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Verified: all ${#expected[@]} assets attached to ${RELEASE_TAG}."

    echo "::error::Could not read the latest stable release, so ${RELEASE_TAG} is not promoted on re-run attempt ${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}."
    exit 1
  fi
fi
if [[ -n "$LATEST" && "$LATEST" != "$RELEASE_TAG" ]] \
  && [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$RELEASE_TAG" "$LATEST" | sort -V | tail -n1)" == "$LATEST" ]]; then

value.name: Promote draft release to published
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
# --latest is gated on the trigger event. On the cascade flow
# (repository_dispatch from release.yml / promote-stable.yml),
# this run is for the freshly-published stable, so re-stamping
# --latest is correct. On the manual recovery flow
# (workflow_dispatch), the operator may be re-running for an
# OLDER tag (e.g., re-uploading assets for v0.4.0 after a later
# v0.5.0 already became Latest). Unconditional --latest there
# silently steals the Latest badge from the newer release.
# Skip --latest on workflow_dispatch; the operator can
# `gh release edit ${RELEASE_TAG} --latest` manually if they
# want to re-claim the badge.
#
# Combined --draft=false [--latest] in one PATCH is empirically
# atomic — GitHub evaluates the make_latest constraint against
# the post-request state, so the draft→published flip and
# Latest stamp succeed in a single call. Beta channel never
# sets --latest.
if [[ "$CHANNEL" == "latest" && "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" != "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
  gh release edit "$RELEASE_TAG" --draft=false --latest
  echo "Promoted ${RELEASE_TAG} to published (draft=false, latest=true; channel=${CHANNEL})."
elif [[ "$CHANNEL" == "latest" ]]; then
  gh release edit "$RELEASE_TAG" --draft=false
  echo "Promoted ${RELEASE_TAG} to published (draft=false, latest=NOT re-stamped because event=workflow_dispatch; channel=${CHANNEL}). Operator: run 'gh release edit ${RELEASE_TAG} --latest' to re-claim Latest if intended."
else
  gh release edit "$RELEASE_TAG" --draft=false
  echo "Promoted ${RELEASE_TAG} to published (draft=false, latest=false; channel=${CHANNEL})."
fi

echo "published=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

value.name: Trigger release.yml to publish stable to npm
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
SELF_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
SINCE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
payload=$(jq -nc \
  --arg ref "$RELEASE_TAG" \
  --arg version "$VERSION" \
  --arg by "$SELF_URL" \
  '{event_type: "publish-stable", client_payload: {ref: $ref, version: $version, dispatched_by: $by}}')
gh api -X POST "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/dispatches" --input - <<<"$payload"
echo "Dispatched publish-stable to release.yml (ref=${RELEASE_TAG}, version=${VERSION}) after the smoke gate + full-inventory verification passed."
# Best-effort forward-link to the release.yml run we just triggered.
CHILD=""
for _ in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  CHILD=$(gh run list --workflow=release.yml --event=repository_dispatch --limit 8 --json url,createdAt \
    --jq "[.[] | select(.createdAt >= \"$SINCE\")] | sort_by(.createdAt) | last | .url // empty" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -n "$CHILD" ]] && break
  sleep 3
done
{
  echo "### Dispatched release.yml (npm publish)"
  echo "- Gated on the DMG smoke verdict: \`${SMOKE_VERDICT}\`"
  if [[ -n "$CHILD" ]]; then echo "- Run: ${CHILD}"; else echo "- (run link unresolved; open release.yml)"; fi
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

value.name: Announce stable release to Slack
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
WEBHOOK_URL="${SLACK_RELEASES_WEBHOOK_URL:-${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}}"
if [[ -z "$WEBHOOK_URL" ]]; then
  echo "::notice::No Slack webhook secret set — skipping Slack announcement for ${RELEASE_TAG}."
  exit 0
fi
RELEASE_URL="https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/tag/${RELEASE_TAG}"
# Inline the notes so the channel reads what shipped without clicking
# through. A failed fetch is not fatal: the builder degrades to the
# header + link message on empty input. The builder strips the
# Downloads block + consumed-set marker on its side.
NOTES="$(timeout --kill-after=5s 30s gh release view "$RELEASE_TAG" --json body --jq '.body' 2>/dev/null)" || NOTES=""
# The builder emits the whole Block Kit payload as JSON (so $VERSION /
# $RELEASE_URL are JSON-escaped — a stray quote in a tag would
# otherwise corrupt the body), converts the notes from GitHub markdown
# to Slack mrkdwn, and keeps every section under Slack's 3000-char cap.
# `text` is the notification/a11y fallback Slack recommends alongside
# blocks. Unit-tested in scripts/build-slack-release-payload.test.mjs.
# This job checked out $GITHUB_SHA, so the builder is always the
# workflow's own copy — no tag-age dance needed here.
payload="$(printf '%s' "$NOTES" \
  | node scripts/build-slack-release-payload.mjs --version "$VERSION" --url "$RELEASE_URL" \
  || true)"
# Never go silent. If the builder fails, post the link-only message
# instead of nothing: losing the notes is a degradation, losing the
# whole announcement is an outage, and the step exiting 0 makes that
# outage invisible.
if [[ -z "$payload" ]]; then
  echo "::warning::Slack notes builder unavailable for ${RELEASE_TAG}; falling back to the link-only announcement."
  payload="$(jq -n \
    --arg version "$VERSION" \
    --arg release_url "$RELEASE_URL" \
    '{
      text: ("OpenKnowledge \($version) released — " + $release_url),
      blocks: [
        { type: "header",
          text: { type: "plain_text", text: "🎉 OpenKnowledge \($version) released", emoji: true } },
        { type: "section",
          text: { type: "mrkdwn",
                  text: ("*<\($release_url)|Release notes & downloads>*") } }
      ]
    }')"
fi
# The failing curl sits in an `if` condition, which `set -e` does
# not treat as fatal — a Slack outage routes to the else/warning
# and the step still exits 0.
if curl -sS --fail --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' --data "$payload" "$WEBHOOK_URL"; then
  echo "Posted stable-release announcement for ${RELEASE_TAG} to Slack."
else
  echo "::warning::Slack announcement failed for ${RELEASE_TAG} (release is published; notification is best-effort)."
fi

if [[ -z "${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL:-}" ]]; then

fi

  --arg version "$VERSION" \
  --arg release_url "$RELEASE_URL" \

      { title: ("OpenKnowledge \($version) released"),

fi

value.name: Hand the re-run to the follower workflow
Alert on a blocked release (FR5c)
value.run:
set -uo pipefail
# A skipped gate (ref predates the harness) is not a blocked release,
# and neither is a failure before the DMG was even built. Both leave
# the verdict empty or 'skipped'; report those as `error` so the
# message never implies the app failed a test it never ran.
#
# A PASS is passed through untouched. The packaging jobs are
# independent, so Linux or Windows can fail while the smoke runs to a
# clean pass — coercing that to `error` is what produced pages reading
# "DMG smoke ERRORED — all 13 executed smoke tests passed".
VERDICT="${SMOKE_VERDICT:-error}"
if [[ "$VERDICT" == "skipped" || -z "$VERDICT" ]]; then
  VERDICT="error"
fi
# Name the jobs that actually FAILED. Downstream jobs that merely
# skipped are consequences, not causes, so they are not listed.
#
# A platform counts only when it is REQUIRED for this cut: under the
# escape valve a non-required platform can fail while publish-assets
# and finalize still run, and naming it would send the responder to a
# job that was correctly excluded from the publish decision — and
# would mask a genuine finalize failure behind it.
REQUIRED="${REQUIRED_PLATFORMS:-mac,windows,linux}"
is_required() { case ",${REQUIRED}," in *",$1,"*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }
blocked=()
[[ "${RESULT_PREPARE}" == "failure" ]] && blocked+=("release preparation")
if [[ "${RESULT_MACOS}" == "failure" || "${RESULT_MACOS}" == "cancelled" ]] && is_required mac; then
  blocked+=("macOS packaging")
fi
if [[ "${RESULT_WINDOWS}" == "failure" || "${RESULT_WINDOWS}" == "cancelled" ]] && is_required windows; then
  blocked+=("Windows packaging")
fi
if [[ "${RESULT_LINUX}" == "failure" || "${RESULT_LINUX}" == "cancelled" ]] && is_required linux; then
  blocked+=("Linux packaging")
fi
[[ "${RESULT_PUBLISH}" == "failure" ]] && blocked+=("asset publication")
# finalize is the alert's own trigger, so it is only worth naming when
# nothing blocking upstream failed — otherwise every page would list it.
if [[ ${#blocked[@]} -eq 0 && ( "${RESULT_FINALIZE}" == "failure" || "${RESULT_FINALIZE}" == "cancelled" ) ]]; then
  blocked+=("finalize")
fi
BLOCKED_BY=""
for b in ${blocked[@]+"${blocked[@]}"}; do
  BLOCKED_BY="${BLOCKED_BY:+${BLOCKED_BY}, }${b}"
done
if [[ "$RESULT_FINALIZE" == "cancelled" && "$BLOCKED_BY" == "finalize" ]]; then
  RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
  TEXT="RELEASE FINALIZATION CANCELLED: ${RELEASE_TAG}: finalize was cancelled. Inspect the Release and run before recovery; publication may have completed. ${RUN_URL}"
  echo "::warning::${TEXT}"
  webhook="${SLACK_RELEASES_WEBHOOK_URL:-${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}}"
  if [[ -n "$webhook" ]]; then
    payload="$(jq -nc --arg text "$TEXT" '{text: $text}')"
    if ! curl -sS --fail --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data "$payload" "$webhook"; then
      echo "::warning::The cancelled-finalize alert failed to POST; inspect the run and Release."
    fi
  fi
  exit 0
fi
REASON="${SMOKE_REASON:-the release pipeline failed before completing — see the run}"
if [[ "${RETRY_OUTCOME:-}" == "failure" ]]; then
  REASON="${REASON}. Not re-run automatically: the re-run decision failed, see the run"
elif [[ "${RETRY_ACTION:-}" == "retry" && "${HANDOFF_OUTCOME:-}" != "success" ]]; then
  REASON="${REASON}. Not re-run automatically: handing the re-run to the follower workflow failed"
elif [[ -n "${RETRY_REASON:-}" ]]; then
  REASON="${REASON}. Not re-run automatically: ${RETRY_REASON}"
fi
RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
post() {
  local webhook="$1" label="$2"
  if [[ -z "$webhook" ]]; then
    echo "::notice::${label} webhook not set — skipping the ${label} smoke alert for ${RELEASE_TAG}."
    return 0
  fi
  local payload=""
  # This job checked out $GITHUB_SHA, so the builder is the
  # workflow's own copy when it exists at all.
  if [[ -f .github/scripts/build-smoke-alert-payload.mjs ]]; then
    payload="$(node .github/scripts/build-smoke-alert-payload.mjs --tag "$RELEASE_TAG" \
      --verdict "$VERDICT" --reason "$REASON" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
      --blocked-by "$BLOCKED_BY" || true)"
  fi
  if [[ -z "$payload" ]]; then
    # Never go silent. Losing the formatting is a degradation; losing
    # the page is the outage this step exists to prevent.
    echo "::warning::Smoke-alert payload builder unavailable for ${RELEASE_TAG}; sending the plain-text alert."
    payload="$(jq -nc --arg t "🚨 RELEASE BLOCKED: ${RELEASE_TAG} — ${BLOCKED_BY:-pipeline ${VERDICT}} — publication may have completed. Inspect the Release, npm and run before recovery. ${REASON} ${RUN_URL}" '{text: $t}')"
  fi
  # The failing curl sits in an `if` condition, so a webhook outage
  # routes to the warning instead of masking the failure.
  if curl -sS --fail --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 30 -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' --data "$payload" "$webhook"; then
    echo "Posted the ${label} smoke alert for ${RELEASE_TAG}."
  else
    echo "::warning::${label} smoke alert failed to POST for ${RELEASE_TAG} — delivery is unconfirmed; inspect the Release, npm and run before recovery."
  fi
}

post "${SLACK_RELEASES_WEBHOOK_URL:-${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}}" Slack
# The annotation is emitted IN ADDITION to the page, so the run page
# tells the same story as the channel.
echo "::error::RELEASE BLOCKED: ${RELEASE_TAG} — ${BLOCKED_BY:-pipeline ${VERDICT}} — ${REASON}. Publication may have completed. Inspect the Release, npm and run before recovery."

value.name: Guard against an in-flight promotion, then dispatch
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
# Don't double-fire while a promote-stable run is already active — covers
# the window between dispatch and promote-stable pushing the stable tag
# (after which the script's stop-at-already-shipped catches it). Fail
# loud on a query error: an evaluator that cannot confirm "no promotion
# in flight" must abort and retry next tick, not assume zero (no
# `|| echo 0`).
active=$(gh run list --workflow=promote-stable.yml --json status \
  --jq '[.[] | select(.status=="in_progress" or .status=="queued")] | length')
if [[ "$active" -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "::notice::A promote-stable run is already in_progress/queued (${active}); skipping to avoid a duplicate promotion."
  exit 0
fi
if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "true" ]]; then
  echo "::notice::DRY RUN: would dispatch promote-stable.yml with beta_tag=${TARGET} (promote-stable computes the stable version)."
  exit 0
fi
# Explicit beta_tag (not blank): a blank dispatch auto-resolves the NEWEST
# beta, but under "latest soaked" the target may sit below the head.
# promote-stable's explicit-tag path skips its own fully-cut guard, so this
# script's unshipped + fully-cut checks are the safety net for this dispatch.
SELF_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
SINCE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
gh workflow run promote-stable.yml -f beta_tag="$TARGET" -f dispatched_by="$SELF_URL"
echo "::notice::Dispatched promote-stable for ${TARGET} (it computes the stable version from the changeset delta, then npm --tag latest + stable DMG)."
# Link this run to the promote-stable run it just created. `gh workflow
# run` does not return the new run id, so resolve it (best-effort) as the
# newest workflow_dispatch run of promote-stable created after SINCE.
CHILD=""
for _ in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
  CHILD=$(gh run list --workflow=promote-stable.yml --event=workflow_dispatch --limit 8 --json url,createdAt \
    --jq "[.[] | select(.createdAt >= \"$SINCE\")] | sort_by(.createdAt) | last | .url // empty" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -n "$CHILD" ]] && break
  sleep 3
done
{
  echo "### Dispatched promote-stable"
  echo "- Beta: \`${TARGET}\`"
  if [[ -n "$CHILD" ]]; then echo "- Run: ${CHILD}"; else echo "- (run link unresolved; open the promote-stable workflow)"; fi
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
if [[ -n "$CHILD" ]]; then echo "::notice::promote-stable run: ${CHILD}"; fi

value.name: Verify the synthetic tree (cherry-pick + fast test tiers)
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
# Drop conflicting refs iteratively instead of aborting the batch: a
# ref that does not apply onto the current stack (stable + earlier
# clean picks) is dropped and the remainder continues — conflicts are
# the common case late in a cycle, and abort-on-first holds every
# clean fix hostage to the oldest drifted one. Each iteration is its
# own single-commit cherry-pick sequence, so --abort unwinds only the
# in-progress pick and keeps earlier survivors on the stack.
IFS=',' read -ra REFS <<< "$FIX_REFS"
SURVIVORS=()
DROPPED=()
# Which paths collided, per dropped ref, as JSON for the refusal page.
# "conflict" alone cannot distinguish a fix that genuinely depends on
# later work from one blocked by an unrelated rewrite of a line of CI
# config, and that is the whole question a reader has.
CONFLICT_JSON='[]'
# Refs whose pick landed empty: the stable already contains the
# change. Not survivors (committing one would re-release), and
# emphatically not conflicts.
ALREADY=()
for ref in "${REFS[@]}"; do
  if git cherry-pick "$ref"; then
    SURVIVORS+=("$ref")
  else
    # BEFORE the abort: --abort clears the index, and with it the
    # unmerged-path list this reads. Capturing after yields nothing.
    # A plain read loop rather than `mapfile` so the shell does not
    # depend on a bash 4 builtin.
    CONFLICTED=()
    while IFS= read -r f; do
      [[ -n "$f" ]] && CONFLICTED+=("$f")
    done < <(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U || true)
    # An EMPTY pick, not a conflict. git exits non-zero for both, but
    # empty means every hunk was already present — the stable already
    # ships this fix under a different SHA, which is how every point
    # release lands. Zero unmerged paths AND a tree identical to HEAD
    # is the signature; a real conflict leaves unmerged paths, and a
    # partial application leaves a dirty tree.
    #
    # Reporting this as a conflict is what made a shipped fix page as
    # "does not apply to the current stable": the refusal carried no
    # conflicting path, and the payload builder fails closed to the
    # severe wording when it has no paths to judge. The containment
    # pre-filter should have caught this upstream; this is the
    # backstop that makes the silence a guarantee rather than a
    # consequence of that filter being right.
    if [[ ${#CONFLICTED[@]} -eq 0 ]] && git diff --quiet HEAD; then
      git cherry-pick --abort || true
      ALREADY+=("$ref")
      echo "::notice::bug-lane: ${ref} is already contained in ${STABLE} (the pick applies empty); skipped — nothing left to ship, and nothing to report."
      continue
    fi
    TOTAL_FILES=$(git show --pretty=format: --name-only "$ref" | grep -c . || true)
    # `${a[@]+"${a[@]}"}` so an empty array is not an unbound-variable
    # error under `set -u`: a pick can fail without conflicting (an
    # empty commit), and that must still mint a report.
    CONFLICT_JSON=$(jq -c \
      --arg ref "$ref" \
      --argjson total "${TOTAL_FILES:-0}" \
      --args '. + [{ref: $ref, totalFiles: $total, conflicts: $ARGS.positional}]' \
      <<< "$CONFLICT_JSON" ${CONFLICTED[@]+"${CONFLICTED[@]}"})
    git cherry-pick --abort || true
    DROPPED+=("$ref")
    echo "::notice::bug-lane: ${ref} does not apply cleanly onto ${STABLE} (conflicted in: ${CONFLICTED[*]:-none}); dropped from this batch — it will ship with its cycle's stable instead."
  fi
done
{
  echo "conflicts<<CONFLICTS_EOF"
  echo "$CONFLICT_JSON"
  echo "CONFLICTS_EOF"
} >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ ${#DROPPED[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "dropped_refs=$(IFS=','; echo "${DROPPED[*]}")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi
if [[ ${#ALREADY[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "already_refs=$(IFS=','; echo "${ALREADY[*]}")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi
if [[ ${#SURVIVORS[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  # Nothing survived AND nothing genuinely conflicted: every candidate
  # was already in the stable. That is a no-op tick, not a refusal —
  # there is no question for a human and therefore no message. A
  # distinct verdict rather than reusing "conflict" is the whole
  # point: the paging steps gate on conflict/fail, so this is silent
  # by construction instead of by a suppression rule someone could
  # later relax. Visible in the run summary for anyone who looks.
  if [[ ${#DROPPED[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "verdict=already-in-stable" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    echo "::notice::bug-lane: every qualifying fix is already contained in ${STABLE}; nothing to ship, nothing to page."
    {
      echo "### Bug lane — already in the stable"
      echo "Every qualifying fix is already contained in \`${STABLE}\`: ${ALREADY[*]}."
      echo "The picks apply empty, so there is nothing left to release. No page — this is a no-op tick, not a refusal."
    } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "verdict=conflict" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "::notice::bug-lane: no qualifying fix is self-contained over ${STABLE}; nothing ships this tick."
  exit 0
fi
SURVIVING_REFS=$(IFS=','; echo "${SURVIVORS[*]}")
echo "surviving_refs=${SURVIVING_REFS}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
if [[ "$SURVIVING_REFS" != "$FIX_REFS" ]]; then
  echo "::notice::bug-lane: continuing with the self-contained subset ${SURVIVING_REFS} (of ${FIX_REFS})."
fi
# The tree that would ship. Fast tiers only: typecheck + unit catch a
# fix that assumed something the stable does not have; the DMG smoke
# later in the cascade covers boot-level integration. An install
# failure must still mint a verdict — an unguarded exit here skips
# the paging step and the refusal disappears into a red-X no one
# watches.
if ! pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; then
  echo "verdict=fail" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "::warning::bug-lane: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile failed on the synthetic tree (${STABLE} + ${SURVIVING_REFS}); treated as a red verification."
  exit 0
fi
if ! { rustup toolchain install --no-self-update && rustc -vV; }; then
  {
    echo "verdict=could-not-verify"
    echo "cause=toolchain"
    echo "failures<<FAILURES_EOF"
    echo '["the declared Rust toolchain could not be installed"]'
    echo "FAILURES_EOF"
  } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "::warning::bug-lane: the declared Rust toolchain could not be installed for ${STABLE} + ${SURVIVING_REFS}. COULD NOT VERIFY, which is not a verdict on the batch."
  exit 0
fi
# `--continue` on the FIRST attempt is what keeps the retry cheap. turbo
# defaults to `--continue=never`: the first failure cancels every
# in-flight and unstarted task, so none of those cache and the retry
# re-runs them too — a failure late in the tiers would cost close to
# two full passes, which this job's wall-clock budget has no room
# for. (The cancel window that once made this urgent belongs to
# bug-lane.yml; since the split this half queues rather than
# cancels, per the group above.) Running the first
# attempt to completion caches every task that genuinely passed, so
# the retry re-executes only what actually failed. `--force` is
# omitted for the same reason: it would discard those cached passes.
# The retry's output is captured because a red verdict has to be able
# to SAY what went red. The refusal page renders per-ref CONFLICT
# evidence under "Why it refused", and a red tier produces no
# conflicts by construction — every survivor picked cleanly, which is
# how it reached the tiers at all. So the most severe verdict was the
# one paging with an empty reason, sending a reader to the run log to
# discover what this step already knew.
#
# `--concurrency=2` caps how many turbo task-graph nodes are
# SCHEDULED at once. It does not reach inside a node: each of the two
# still runs its Vitest fork pool at the default width, so the shape
# is two supervisors sharing four cores, not the one-tier-per-box the
# PR tier gets. A fivefold cut from turbo's default of ten, which is
# not the same thing as isolation.
#
# The workspace does own a cap that WOULD reach the pools --
# `boundedMaxForks` in test-support/vitest.base.ts -- and it cannot
# help here: it applies only when `!CI && cpuCount >= 8`, and this
# runner fails BOTH halves. Widening the `CI` guard alone would change
# nothing on a four-core box, which is why the bound has to come from
# this side instead.
RETRY_LOG="${RUNNER_TEMP}/bug-lane-tiers-retry.log"
# Created up front because a first-attempt blow skips the retry
# entirely, and the extraction below reads this file either way.
: > "$RETRY_LOG"
# The tiers carry their own ceiling because the job's is a hard kill:
# it sets no verdict, and every paging step below gates on one, so a
# tick that hits it refuses NOTHING. And nothing queues behind it:
# bug-lane.yml declines to dispatch while a verify is in flight, so
# the ~20-minute ticks in that window evaluate and skip, and the lane
# simply stops verifying for as long as the wedge lasts. Wrapping
# turns that into exit 124, which this step can report and the page
# can render.
#
# Sized from the one measurement taken on THIS runner: the last
# unbounded tick spent 1460s in this step, covering cherry-pick,
# install and BOTH attempts, which bounds a single attempt well under
# 1500s without measuring it directly.
#
# The bounded single-attempt cost is still unmeasured -- it needs a
# dispatch of this workflow -- and it is the number to re-check if a
# tick ever runs out of budget. Both attempts carry this ceiling, so the bound
# is 2x1500s, about 50 minutes against the job's 60 -- the remaining
# ten cover checkout, setup, the cherry-pick loop and the install,
# none of which are bounded themselves.
TIER_BUDGET_SECONDS=1500
FIRST_STATUS=0
timeout --foreground --kill-after=10s "${TIER_BUDGET_SECONDS}s" \
  pnpm exec turbo run typecheck test test:uncached --concurrency=2 --continue --output-logs=errors-only --log-prefix=none \
  || FIRST_STATUS=$?
RETRY_STATUS=0
if [[ "$FIRST_STATUS" -ne 0 ]]; then
  case "$FIRST_STATUS" in
    124|137)
      RETRY_STATUS="$FIRST_STATUS"
      ;;
    *)
      if timeout --foreground --kill-after=10s "${TIER_BUDGET_SECONDS}s" \
        pnpm exec turbo run typecheck test test:uncached --concurrency=2 --output-logs=errors-only --log-prefix=none 2>&1 | tee "$RETRY_LOG"; then
        RETRY_STATUS=0
      else
        # Read BEFORE any other command: the next one clobbers it.
        RETRY_STATUS="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
      fi
      ;;
  esac
fi
# 124 is timeout's own signal, 137 the SIGKILL that --kill-after
# escalates to. Reading it here is sufficient because a blow is never
# retried: reaching the retry at all implies attempt 1 failed the
# ordinary way, so this is whichever attempt produced the verdict.
#
# It becomes its OWN verdict rather than riding `fail` with a flag
# beside it. The page, the refusal signature and the step gates all
# key on the verdict, so a flag has to be threaded to each of them
# separately -- and one wiring mistake is silent, because every reader
# defaults it. A verdict cannot be half-delivered that way.
TIER_VERDICT=fail
case "$RETRY_STATUS" in 124|137) TIER_VERDICT=could-not-verify ;; esac
if [[ "$FIRST_STATUS" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "verdict=pass" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
elif [[ "$RETRY_STATUS" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "verdict=pass" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "::warning::bug-lane: fast tiers passed on retry for ${STABLE} + ${SURVIVING_REFS} — the first attempt failed (flake-class); see its log before trusting this tick."
else
  echo "verdict=${TIER_VERDICT}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  # Vitest names the failing test on a `FAIL` line. A typecheck-only
  # failure produces none, so fall back to turbo's own failed-task
  # lines rather than paging empty again. Sorted-unique and capped:
  # the page is a pointer to the log, not a copy of it. Extraction is
  # inline shell and not a helper script on purpose — this step runs
  # against the SYNTHETIC tree, detached at the stable, where a script
  # added after that stable was cut does not exist.
  # The ESC is built with printf rather than written as `\x1b`, which
  # only GNU sed understands — the runner has GNU sed today, and a
  # silent no-op on any host that does not would strip nothing and
  # leave every extracted name wrapped in escape codes.
  ESC="$(printf '\033')"
  strip_ansi() { sed -e "s/${ESC}\[[0-9;]*m//g" "$RETRY_LOG"; }
  # The 200 cap is a runaway bound, not the page's display limit —
  # the page shows a handful and computes "…and N more" from what it
  # receives, so a cap tight enough to bite would silently understate
  # that remainder. A red tier producing 200 distinct failures is a
  # broken base, not a fix, and the count is a floor at that point.
  FAILURES="$(strip_ansi | grep -E '^[[:space:]]*FAIL[[:space:]]' \
    | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]*FAIL[[:space:]]+//' | sort -u | head -200 || true)"
  if [[ -z "$FAILURES" ]]; then
    # Anchored on turbo's `<pkg>#<task>:` prefix, which is the only
    # one of its three exit lines that names the task that failed.
    # Measured against the pinned turbo, one failing task emits
    # `::error::command (…) exited (1)`, `<pkg>#<task>:  ERROR  command
    # (…) exited (1)` and ` ERROR  run failed: command  exited (1)`: a
    # bare `command .* exited` match yields three bullets for one
    # failure, two of them redundant and one naming nothing at all.
    FAILURES="$(strip_ansi | grep -E '#[^ ]+:.*exited \([0-9]+\)' | sort -u | head -200 || true)"
  fi
  # A budget blow names no test, so the extraction above has nothing
  # to find. Saying that outright is the point of separating it: the
  # incident this lane exists to avoid is a refusal that blames a fix
  # for something the runner did. Defaulted so the block above stays
  # liftable and runnable on its own.
  if [[ "${TIER_VERDICT:-fail}" == "could-not-verify" ]]; then
    # Just the fact. The page's own framing carries what it means,
    # in the meaning line and again in the options, and rendering all
    # three showed the same sentence three times over.
    FAILURES="the tiers did not finish within ${TIER_BUDGET_SECONDS}s (exit ${RETRY_STATUS})"
  fi
  # Encoded into a variable BEFORE the heredoc block, with a fallback.
  # Under `set -e` a jq that exits non-zero mid-block (invalid UTF-8
  # surviving in the captured log, say) would abort between the
  # `failures<<` line and its terminator, leaving an unterminated
  # multiline block in $GITHUB_OUTPUT and failing the step — and the
  # paging step has no `if: always()`, so the refusal would vanish
  # silently. That is precisely the failure mode this whole change
  # exists to remove, so it must not be reintroduced by its own
  # plumbing.
  FAILURES_JSON="$(printf '%s\n' "$FAILURES" | jq -cRn '[inputs | select(length > 0)]' || echo '[]')"
  {
    echo "failures<<FAILURES_EOF"
    printf '%s\n' "$FAILURES_JSON"
    echo "FAILURES_EOF"
  } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  # Says what is known and stops there. The previous wording asserted
  # the fix assumed something the stable lacks, which is only one of
  # the causes: a tier can equally be red because the stable's own
  # tree is red, and reading a base failure as an incompatible fix is
  # how a lane-wide outage looks like a series of bad fixes.
  if [[ "${TIER_VERDICT:-fail}" == "could-not-verify" ]]; then
    echo "::warning::bug-lane: fast tiers ran out of budget on ${STABLE} + ${SURVIVING_REFS} — COULD NOT VERIFY, which is not a verdict on the batch. What ran out is the clock; whether that is the runner or the tree, this tick cannot say. It stays on its cycle's path."
  else
    echo "::warning::bug-lane: fast tiers failed TWICE on ${STABLE} + ${SURVIVING_REFS} — not flake-class. Either the fix assumes something the stable does not have, or the stable is red on its own; the named failures below decide which. It stays on its cycle's path."
  fi
fi

value.name: Dispatch the point release (or log what would ship)
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
if [[ "${BUG_LANE_ARMED}" != "true" ]]; then
  echo "::notice::bug-lane LOG-ONLY: would dispatch point-release (cherry-pick) of ${FIX_REFS} over ${STABLE}."
  {
    echo "### Bug lane — log-only"
    echo "- Would point-release: \`${FIX_REFS}\` over \`${STABLE}\` (verify passed)"
  } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  exit 0
fi
# Re-check just before dispatching: the earlier in-flight check is
# ~15 minutes stale after the verify stage, and a promotion may have
# started meanwhile. point-release's shared concurrency group would
# serialize anyway; this avoids queuing a release that the next tick
# would have re-derived against the newer stable.
active=0
for wf in point-release.yml promote-stable.yml; do
  n=$(gh run list --workflow="$wf" --json status \
    --jq '[.[] | select(.status=="in_progress" or .status=="queued")] | length')
  active=$((active + n))
done
if [[ "$active" -gt 0 ]]; then
  echo "::notice::bug-lane: a release run started during verify (${active}); retrying next tick."
  exit 0
fi
SELF_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
gh workflow run point-release.yml \
  -f mode=cherry-pick -f fix_refs="$FIX_REFS" -f dry_run=false -f dispatched_by="$SELF_URL"
echo "::notice::bug-lane: dispatched point-release (cherry-pick) of ${FIX_REFS} over ${STABLE}."

value.name: Drop signature
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
sig="$(printf '%s|%s' "$DROPPED_REFS" "$SURVIVING_REFS" | sha256sum | cut -c1-32)"
echo "sig=${sig}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "marker=${RUNNER_TEMP}/bug-lane-drop-marker" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

value.name: Has this drop already been paged?
Note a suppressed drop
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
{
  echo "### Bug lane — drop still standing, page suppressed"
  echo "Dropped \`${DROPPED_REFS}\`, signature \`${SIG}\`, already paged on an earlier tick."
  echo "The channel stays quiet by design; this re-pages only if the dropped or dispatched set changes."
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "::notice::bug-lane: drop ${SIG} already paged; suppressing the duplicate page."

value.name: Notify on a partial drop (armed only)
value.run:
set -uo pipefail
# `delivered` is the ONLY thing the markers may key on, so it is
# written on EVERY path — no early exit. An unset output and an
# explicit 'false' both fail the `== 'true'` gate today, so this is
# inert either way; it is written out because the contract is what
# the markers depend on, and an implicit GHA default is a thinner
# thing to depend on than a value this step always states. Same shape
# as the refusal step below, deliberately.
delivered=false
WEBHOOK_URL="${SLACK_RELEASES_WEBHOOK_URL:-${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}}"
if [[ -z "$WEBHOOK_URL" ]]; then
  echo "::notice::No Slack webhook secret set — drop notification skipped."
else
  RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
  TEXT="⚠️ Bug lane dropped ${DROPPED_REFS} (cherry-pick conflict with ${STABLE}); they ride their cycle's 24h path — investigate whether any needs a manual point release. Dispatched the self-contained subset ${SURVIVING_REFS}. ${RUN_URL}"
  payload="$(jq -nc --arg t "$TEXT" '{text: $t}')"
  if curl -sS --fail -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' --data "$payload" "$WEBHOOK_URL"; then
    delivered=true
  else
    echo "::warning::bug-lane drop notification failed to POST — the dispatch itself is unaffected, and the drop stays un-marked so the next tick pages it again."
  fi
fi
echo "delivered=${delivered}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

value.name: Record that this drop was paged
value.run: printf '%s\n' "${{ steps.drop.outputs.sig }}" > "${{ steps.drop.outputs.marker }}"

value.name: A tick that produced no verdict is still a refusal
value.run: echo "::warning::bug-lane: verify produced no verdict for ${STABLE} — COULD NOT VERIFY. Nothing here is evidence about the queued fixes; read the run log for where it stopped."

value.name: Refusal signature
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
if ! git show "${GITHUB_SHA}:.github/scripts/bug-lane-refusal-key.mjs" > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/bug-lane-refusal-key.mjs" \
  || ! sig="$(node "${RUNNER_TEMP}/bug-lane-refusal-key.mjs")"; then
  echo "::warning::Could not group the refusal; retaining batch-based paging."
  sig="$(printf '%s|%s|%s' "$VERDICT" "$FIX_REFS" "$SURVIVING_REFS" | sha256sum | cut -c1-32)"
fi
echo "sig=${sig}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "marker=${RUNNER_TEMP}/bug-lane-refusal-marker" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

value.name: Has this refusal already been paged?
Note a suppressed refusal
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
{
  echo "### Bug lane — refusal still standing, page suppressed"
  echo "Verdict \`${VERDICT}\`, signature \`${SIG}\`, already paged on an earlier tick."
  echo "For named verification failures, grouping is per stable and failing suite for the UTC day. Conflicts, could-not-verify ticks and unnamed failures use verdict and batch identity. Batch details remain in each run."
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
echo "::notice::bug-lane: refusal ${SIG} already paged; suppressing the duplicate page."

value.name: Page on a refusal (armed only)
value.run:
set -uo pipefail
# `delivered` is the ONLY thing the marker may key on. The step's own
# conclusion cannot stand in for it: a dead webhook is downgraded to
# a warning (losing a notification must never fail a release job), and
# an unset secret exits early, so this step reports success in both
# cases while nothing reached anyone.
delivered=false
WEBHOOK_URL="${SLACK_RELEASES_WEBHOOK_URL:-${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}}"
if [[ -z "$WEBHOOK_URL" ]]; then
  echo "::notice::No Slack webhook secret set — refusal page skipped."
else
  RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
  # The verify step left the workspace detached at the stable tag,
  # which predates this tooling — every step shares one workspace, so
  # the builder below is simply absent from disk. Restore the lane's
  # own scripts from the ref the workflow is running from. Restored
  # per path, never as one pathspec: `git checkout <ref> -- a b` is
  # atomic, so a path missing at that ref would silently take the
  # other one down with it and leave the page permanently degraded.
  # The synthetic tree has already served its purpose here — verify
  # is done, and dispatch (which reads no repo file) is mutually
  # exclusive with this step.
  for p in .github/scripts scripts; do
    git checkout "$GITHUB_SHA" -- "$p" 2>/dev/null \
      || echo "::warning::bug-lane: could not restore ${p}; the page may fall back."
  done
  # Defaults go through intermediate variables, NOT `${V:-{\}}`: a
  # brace in a parameter-expansion default is taken literally
  # (backslash and all), so jq --argjson would reject it and every
  # page would silently degrade to the fallback below.
  TICKETS_JSON="${FIX_TICKETS:-}"
  [[ -z "$TICKETS_JSON" ]] && TICKETS_JSON='{}'
  CONFLICTS_JSON="${CONFLICTS:-}"
  [[ -z "$CONFLICTS_JSON" ]] && CONFLICTS_JSON='[]'
  FAILURES_JSON="${FAILURES:-}"
  [[ -z "$FAILURES_JSON" ]] && FAILURES_JSON='[]'
  # Join each dropped ref to the tickets that qualified it, so the
  # page names the bug rather than only a SHA.
  INPUT="$(jq -nc \
    --arg verdict "$VERDICT" \
    --arg cause "${CAUSE:-}" \
    --arg stable "$STABLE" \
    --arg runUrl "$RUN_URL" \
    --argjson conflicts "$CONFLICTS_JSON" \
    --argjson failures "$FAILURES_JSON" \
    --argjson tickets "$TICKETS_JSON" \
    '{verdict: $verdict, cause: $cause, stable: $stable, runUrl: $runUrl, failures: $failures,
      refs: [$conflicts[] | . + {tickets: ($tickets[.ref] // [])}]}')"
  # A page that cannot be composed must not become silence: fall back
  # to the bare facts rather than skipping the POST, and leave the
  # marker unwritten so the next tick tries again.
  if ! payload="$(node .github/scripts/bug-lane-refusal-payload.mjs --input "$INPUT")"; then
    echo "::warning::bug-lane: could not compose the refusal page; falling back to a plain message."
    payload="$(jq -nc --arg t "Bug lane: ${FIX_REFS} did not ship in the fast lane (${VERDICT}) over ${STABLE}. ${RUN_URL}" '{text: $t}')"
  fi
  if curl -sS --fail -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' --data "$payload" "$WEBHOOK_URL"; then
    delivered=true
  else
    echo "::warning::bug-lane refusal page failed to POST — the refusal still holds and stays un-marked, so the next tick pages it again."
  fi
fi
echo "delivered=${delivered}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

value.name: Record that this refusal was paged
value.run: printf '%s\n' "${{ steps.refusal.outputs.sig }}" > "${{ steps.refusal.outputs.marker }}"

value.name: Fail the run on a refusing verdict
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
case "$VERDICT" in
  conflict|fail|could-not-verify)
    echo "::error::bug-lane: verdict ${VERDICT} refuses this batch, so the run concludes failure."
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

settings.value: Beta tag to promote (e.g., v0.4.0-beta.3). Leave blank to promote the newest beta.
URL of the run that dispatched this promotion (run-to-run link). Blank for manual runs.

value.name: Resolve beta tag to promote
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
if [[ -n "${INPUT_BETA_TAG:-}" ]]; then
  RESOLVED="$INPUT_BETA_TAG"
  echo "auto=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "Using explicitly provided beta tag: $RESOLVED"
else
  RESOLVED=$(git tag --list 'v*-beta.*' --sort=-version:refname \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-beta\.[0-9]+$' \
    | head -n 1 || true)
  if [[ -z "$RESOLVED" ]]; then
    echo "::error::No vX.Y.Z-beta.N tags found to promote. Did the auto-cadence beta release run?"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "auto=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "Auto-resolved newest beta tag: $RESOLVED"
fi
echo "beta_tag=$RESOLVED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

value.name: Verify beta tag exists
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
if ! git rev-parse "refs/tags/${BETA_TAG}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "::error::Beta tag '${BETA_TAG}' not found on the public repo. Did the auto-cadence release run?"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Tag ${BETA_TAG} resolves to $(git rev-parse "refs/tags/${BETA_TAG}")"

value.name: Install root dependencies for the Changesets reader
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
corepack enable
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter=. --ignore-scripts

set -euo pipefail
node scripts/compute-stable-version.mjs "$BETA_TAG"

value.name: Read the release-note level of every changeset the stable ships
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
node scripts/render-stable-notes.mjs --read-levels --commit "$BETA_SHA"

value.name: Resolve beta tag to promote
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
if [[ -n "${INPUT_BETA_TAG:-}" ]]; then
  RESOLVED="$INPUT_BETA_TAG"
  echo "auto=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "Using explicitly provided beta tag: $RESOLVED"
else
  RESOLVED=$(git tag --list 'v*-beta.*' --sort=-version:refname \
    | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-beta\.[0-9]+$' \
    | head -n 1 || true)
  if [[ -z "$RESOLVED" ]]; then
    echo "::error::No vX.Y.Z-beta.N tags found to promote. Did the auto-cadence beta release run?"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "auto=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "Auto-resolved newest beta tag: $RESOLVED"
fi
echo "beta_tag=$RESOLVED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

value.name: Refuse bumps read for a different beta
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
if [[ "$RESOLVED" != "$READ_BUMPS_BETA_TAG" ]]; then
  echo "::error::read-bumps read changeset bumps for '${READ_BUMPS_BETA_TAG}', but this job resolved '${RESOLVED}'. Refusing to promote with bumps read for a different beta. This usually means only the failed jobs were re-run after a newer beta landed, which reuses read-bumps' earlier result. Re-run all jobs, or dispatch promote-stable with an explicit beta_tag."
  exit 1
fi
echo "read-bumps read the same beta this job resolved: ${RESOLVED}"

value.name: Guard - auto-resolved beta is fully cut
value.run:
set -euo pipefail

# Guard B — the beta cut must be COMPLETE. release.yml creates the
# beta Release as --draft; desktop-release.yml flips it to published
# ONLY after the signed DMG + beta-mac.yml upload succeeds, and it
# runs on a SEPARATE concurrency group, so promote-stable can
# otherwise acquire the release lock while the DMG is still building
# (up to 45 min). npm beta publish happens earlier in the same
# pipeline, so a published release implies the npm artifact too. A
# draft or asset-less release = the cut is in-flight or failed;
# promoting it would build stable from an unvalidated SHA.
meta=$(gh release view "$BETA_TAG" --json isDraft,assets 2>/dev/null || true)
if [[ -z "$meta" ]]; then
  echo "::error::No GitHub Release exists for ${BETA_TAG} yet — its beta cut has not finished creating the release. Wait for the cut to complete, then retry."
  exit 1
fi
isDraft=$(printf '%s' "$meta" | jq -r '.isDraft')
dmg=$(printf '%s' "$meta" | jq -r '[.assets[].name | select(endswith(".dmg"))] | length')
manifest=$(printf '%s' "$meta" | jq -r '[.assets[].name | select(endswith("-mac.yml"))] | length')
if [[ "$isDraft" == "true" || "$dmg" -eq 0 || "$manifest" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "::error::Beta ${BETA_TAG} is not fully cut (draft=${isDraft}, dmg=${dmg}, mac.yml=${manifest}). Its desktop-release build is still running or failed — wait a few minutes and retry, or fix the failed cut before promoting."
  exit 1
fi
echo "Beta ${BETA_TAG} is complete (published, ${dmg} dmg, ${manifest} mac.yml); safe to promote."

value.name: Compute stable version from beta tag
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
# Compute the stable version as a SINGLE semver bump over the current
# latest stable, from the changeset delta between that stable's SHA and
# this beta's SHA — NOT by stripping -beta.N. Stripping collapsed every
# beta in a cycle to one stable, so a later beta could never promote and
# a manual re-promote collided with the existing vX.Y.Z tag. This script
# is the single source of version truth for manual + auto promotions; it
# writes skip / stable_version / stable_tag / beta_sha / latest_stable_sha
# to $GITHUB_OUTPUT. skip=true is a clean no-op (the beta is already
# shipped, or adds no changesets) and gates every step below.
node scripts/compute-stable-version.mjs "$BETA_TAG"

value.name: Refuse a stable that carries the release hold
value.run: node .github/scripts/release-hold.mjs --candidate "$BETA_SHA" --label "${STABLE_TAG} from ${BETA_TAG}" --main HEAD

value.name: Refuse a stable that lacks a fix a published stable shipped
value.run: node .github/scripts/shipped-fix-containment.mjs --candidate "$BETA_SHA" --label "${STABLE_TAG} from ${BETA_TAG}"

value.name: Link to triggering run
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
if [[ -n "${DISPATCHED_BY:-}" ]]; then
  echo "::notice::Triggered by ${DISPATCHED_BY}"
  { echo "### Triggered by"; echo "- ${DISPATCHED_BY}"; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
else
  echo "Triggered manually or by external repository_dispatch." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi

value.name: Render release notes from the stable's changesets
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
BODY_FILE=$(mktemp)
node scripts/render-stable-notes.mjs --commit "$BETA_SHA" --exclude-tag "$STABLE_TAG" > "$BODY_FILE"

if [[ ! -s "$BODY_FILE" ]]; then
  printf 'No changelog entries.\n' > "$BODY_FILE"
fi

MAX_BODY=120000
if [[ $(wc -c < "$BODY_FILE") -gt $MAX_BODY ]]; then
  echo "Release notes are $(wc -c < "$BODY_FILE") chars, over ${MAX_BODY}; truncating."
  TRUNC=$(mktemp)
  # Cut at MAX_BODY bytes, then drop the (now-partial) last line.
  head -c "$MAX_BODY" "$BODY_FILE" | sed '$d' > "$TRUNC"
  {
    printf '\n\n---\n\n'
    printf '_Changelog truncated to fit GitHub'\''s 125,000-character release-body limit. '
    printf 'The notes for every release are at https://github.com/%s/releases_\n' "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
  } >> "$TRUNC"
  mv "$TRUNC" "$BODY_FILE"
fi

echo "body_file=$BODY_FILE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "---- Release body preview ----"
cat "$BODY_FILE"
echo "------------------------------"

value.name: Tag stable at beta SHA
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

# Idempotency: a re-run after a transient failure should not
# explode if the tag already exists.

else

value.name: Create stable GitHub Release
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
# Idempotency: a re-run after a transient failure should not
# explode if the Release already exists.
if gh release view "$STABLE_TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Release ${STABLE_TAG} already exists; updating notes and preserving publication state."
  gh release edit "$STABLE_TAG" --notes-file "$BODY_FILE"
else
  # Create as draft so the release is invisible in the .atom feed
  # until desktop-release.yml uploads latest-mac.yml AND promotes
  # draft → published. --latest is deferred to the promote step
  # because GitHub's API rejects make_latest=true on drafts. See
  # packages/desktop/src/main/auto-updater.ts:336-356 for the
  # channel-mirror invariant this protects.
  gh release create "$STABLE_TAG" \
    --draft \
    --target "$BETA_SHA" \
    --title "$STABLE_TAG" \
    --notes-file "$BODY_FILE"
fi

value.name: Trigger desktop-release.yml to build + upload stable DMG
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
SELF_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
SINCE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
payload=$(jq -nc \
  --arg tag "$STABLE_TAG" \
  --arg ref "$STABLE_TAG" \
  --arg by "$SELF_URL" \
  '{event_type: "desktop-release", client_payload: {release_tag: $tag, ref: $ref, dispatched_by: $by}}')
gh api -X POST "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/dispatches" --input - <<<"$payload"
echo "Dispatched desktop-release for ${STABLE_TAG}; desktop-release.yml will build the signed DMG and upload it + latest-mac.yml to the stable Release."
# Best-effort forward-link to the desktop-release.yml run we just triggered.
CHILD=""
for _ in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  CHILD=$(gh run list --workflow=desktop-release.yml --event=repository_dispatch --limit 8 --json url,createdAt \
    --jq "[.[] | select(.createdAt >= \"$SINCE\")] | sort_by(.createdAt) | last | .url // empty" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -n "$CHILD" ]] && break
  sleep 3
done
{
  echo "### Dispatched desktop-release.yml (signed DMG)"
  if [[ -n "$CHILD" ]]; then echo "- Run: ${CHILD}"; else echo "- (run link unresolved; open desktop-release.yml)"; fi
  echo "- That run smokes the DMG, promotes the draft Release, then dispatches publish-stable to release.yml for npm. npm \`latest\` does NOT move until the smoke passes."
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# the page names both rather than guessing which one happened.

  OUTCOME="was cancelled or timed out"
else
  OUTCOME="failed"
fi
TEXT="Linear release stamping ${OUTCOME} for ${TAG}${CHANNEL:+ (${CHANNEL})}. The release itself is unaffected; Linear is now out of sync with what shipped. Re-running is safe for transient failures. After a stamping-code fix reaches main, dispatch linear-release.yml fresh on main with release_tag=${TAG}; re-running the old run keeps its old code. Stable dispatches re-verify every stable release's stamps, not just this one. ${RUN_URL}"
if [[ "${LINEAR_KEY_REJECTED:-}" == "true" ]]; then
  TEXT="Linear release stamping failed for ${TAG}${CHANNEL:+ (${CHANNEL})}: Linear rejected the LINEAR_API_KEY secret on ${GITHUB_REPOSITORY} with HTTP 401, so the key has expired or been revoked. Re-running will not help and no code fix is needed. Create a new key in Linear (Settings > Security & access > Personal API keys) on a shared account, with Read and Write permissions (Admin is not needed) on all teams, store it with gh secret set LINEAR_API_KEY -R ${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}, then dispatch linear-release.yml fresh on main with release_tag=${TAG}. Reporter write-back uses the same key, so it is failing too. ${RUN_URL}"
fi
{

  echo "Tag: \`${TAG}\`"
  echo "Run: ${RUN_URL}"
} >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# job, so both the missing-secret and dead-webhook paths warn and
# return success — the red run is still the underlying alert.
WEBHOOK_URL="${SLACK_RELEASES_WEBHOOK_URL:-${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL:-}}"
if [[ -z "$WEBHOOK_URL" ]]; then
  echo "::warning::No Slack webhook secret is configured; the workflow failure remains the alert."

fi
