value.run:
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
KEYCHAIN_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/ok-signing.keychain-db"
KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD="$(head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64)"
echo "::add-mask::$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD"
CERT_PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/ok-signing.p12"
trap 'rm -f "$CERT_PATH"' EXIT

# CSC_LINK is bare base64 of the .p12 (workflow header). macOS
# `base64 -i` wraps lines, hence the whitespace strip.
printf '%s' "$CSC_LINK" | tr -d '[:space:]' | base64 -d > "$CERT_PATH"
if [[ ! -s "$CERT_PATH" ]]; then
  echo "::error::CSC_LINK did not materialize a .p12 (empty after decode). Re-export with 'base64 -i developer-id.p12 | pbcopy' and paste the single-line output."
  exit 1
fi

security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN_PATH"
# No lock timeout: sign + notarize runs well past the 5 min default.
security set-keychain-settings "$KEYCHAIN_PATH"
security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN_PATH"
security import "$CERT_PATH" -k "$KEYCHAIN_PATH" -P "$CSC_KEY_PASSWORD" \
  -T /usr/bin/codesign -T /usr/bin/productbuild >/dev/null
# The call electron-builder gets wrong: -k is the KEYCHAIN password.
# Without this, codesign blocks on a GUI prompt for the private key.
security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s \
  -k "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN_PATH" >/dev/null

# Search list: this keychain first, then electron-builder's bundled
# Apple root + intermediate certs (it adds these itself on the
# CSC_LINK path so the Developer ID chain validates offline), then
# whatever was already listed. `list-keychains -s` REPLACES the list.
ROOT_CERTS="$(node -e '
  const path = require("path");
  const eb = path.dirname(require.resolve("electron-builder/package.json"));
  const lib = path.dirname(require.resolve("app-builder-lib/package.json", { paths: [eb] }));
  process.stdout.write(path.join(lib, "certs", "root_certs.keychain"));
')"
if [[ ! -f "$ROOT_CERTS" ]]; then
  echo "::error::app-builder-lib's bundled root_certs.keychain is not at $ROOT_CERTS; its certs layout may have moved in a dependency bump."
  exit 1
fi
if ! LISTED="$(security list-keychains -d user)"; then
  echo "::error::security list-keychains failed; refusing to replace the user search list blind."
  exit 1
fi
EXISTING=()
while IFS= read -r line; do
  line="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
  line="${line%\"}"
  line="${line#\"}"
  [[ -n "$line" ]] && EXISTING+=("$line")
done <<<"$LISTED"
# `${arr[@]+...}`: the runner's bash 3.2 treats an empty array as
# unbound under set -u.
security list-keychains -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN_PATH" "$ROOT_CERTS" ${EXISTING[@]+"${EXISTING[@]}"}

IDENTITIES="$(security find-identity -v -p codesigning "$KEYCHAIN_PATH")"

value.name: Sync to the packages bucket
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
if [ -z "$BUCKET" ] || [ -z "$ENDPOINT" ]; then
  echo "::error::LINUX_REPO_BUCKET var / LINUX_REPO_R2_ENDPOINT secret not set — see scripts/linux-repo/README.md"
  exit 1
fi
# Upload-first, prune-last — the repo is LIVE during the sync. A
# client that fetched the OLD index must still find the OLD pool
# files until the NEW index is up, so:
#   1. pool/packages WITHOUT --delete (old + new coexist briefly);
#   2. metadata (dists/, repodata/) — points at the new files,
#      which step 1 guaranteed are present;
#   3. prune pass with --delete, now that no live index references
#      the old files.
# --delete stays scoped to this channel's prefixes, which is what
# keeps the bucket latest-only per channel without touching the
# sibling channel.
sync() { aws s3 sync --endpoint-url "$ENDPOINT" --no-progress "$@"; }
if [ -d "/tmp/repo/apt/pool/$CHANNEL" ]; then
  sync "/tmp/repo/apt/pool/$CHANNEL"  "s3://$BUCKET/apt/pool/$CHANNEL"
fi
if [ -d "/tmp/repo/rpm/$CHANNEL" ]; then
  sync "/tmp/repo/rpm/$CHANNEL" "s3://$BUCKET/rpm/$CHANNEL"
fi
if [ -d "/tmp/repo/apt/dists/$CHANNEL" ]; then
  sync --delete "/tmp/repo/apt/dists/$CHANNEL" "s3://$BUCKET/apt/dists/$CHANNEL"
fi
if [ -d "/tmp/repo/apt/pool/$CHANNEL" ]; then
  sync --delete "/tmp/repo/apt/pool/$CHANNEL"  "s3://$BUCKET/apt/pool/$CHANNEL"
fi
if [ -d "/tmp/repo/rpm/$CHANNEL" ]; then
  sync --delete "/tmp/repo/rpm/$CHANNEL" "s3://$BUCKET/rpm/$CHANNEL"
fi
# Public keys: tiny, immutable in practice, never --delete.
[ -f /tmp/repo/apt/openknowledge.gpg ] && sync /tmp/repo/apt "s3://$BUCKET/apt" --exclude 'dists/*' --exclude 'pool/*'
[ -f /tmp/repo/rpm/key.asc ] && aws s3 cp --endpoint-url "$ENDPOINT" /tmp/repo/rpm/key.asc "s3://$BUCKET/rpm/key.asc"
